question_text: Nitko and Brookhart (2007) described assessment as:
option_b: A process for obtaining information used for making decisions about students, curricula, and educational policy
option_d: A synonym for evaluation with no distinction
explanation: Nitko and Brookhart (2007) described assessment as a process for obtaining information used for making decisions about students, curricula, programme, schools, and educational policy.

question_text: Classroom assessment is generally divided into three types in this unit. Which of the following is one of them?
explanation: The three types are: assessment for learning (formative), assessment of learning (summative), and assessment as learning.

question_text: Assessment that is cumulative in nature, confirming what students already know at the end of a unit or session, is called:
explanation: Assessment of learning (summative assessment) is cumulative, confirming what students know at the end of one or more units of study.

question_text: Which term refers to the process of making a value judgement about the worth of a student's product or performance?
explanation: Evaluation is the process of making a value judgement about the worth of a student's product or performance.

question_text: The purpose of assessment concerned with assigning learners to different levels of the same general instruction, with no one rejected, is called:
explanation: Placement assigns people to different levels of the same general type of instruction, education, or work -- no one is rejected.

question_text: The purpose of assessment concerned with confirming that a learner has met minimum competency to receive a certificate is called:
explanation: Credentialing and Certification involves assessment used to ascertain whether a learner has met minimum competency to be given a certificate.

question_text: In NOUN, how many computer-marked assignments (CMAs) does each student take per course, per the figures given in this unit?
explanation: Each student takes four computer-marked assignments of eighty (80) multiple-choice items total, broken into 20 items per assignment.

question_text: Assignments submitted to an instructor who scores and grades them based on set criteria are called:
explanation: Tutor-marked assignment (TMA) is given to learners and submitted to the instructor/facilitator who scores and grades it based on set criteria.

question_text: According to this unit, why is self-assessment described as having little meaning without transparent, understood learning goals?
option_a: Because students cannot effectively evaluate performance without knowing what the targets are
option_c: Because only tutors can assess performance
option_d: Because self-assessment is banned in ODL
explanation: Without knowing what the learning targets are, a student could not effectively evaluate their performance -- transparency of goals is essential.

question_text: In NOUN, which levels take the Pen-on-Paper (PoP) examination, as described in this unit?
option_b: 300, 400, 500 level undergraduates and postgraduates (plus Faculty of Law)
explanation: PoP examinations are for undergraduates in 300, 400, 500 levels, Faculty of Law students, and all postgraduate students.

question_text: Which levels of undergraduate students (excluding Faculty of Law) take electronic examinations (e-exams) in NOUN?
explanation: Electronic examination (e-exam) is for undergraduates in 100 and 200 levels, except those from the Faculty of Law.

question_text: According to Northedge (2010), which of the following is something to AVOID when writing an examination?
option_b: Not answering the question due to failing to recognise key terms
explanation: Not answering the question -- failing to recognise the key terms and issues -- is listed as a mistake to avoid, per Northedge (2010).

question_text: Examination is described in this unit as serving which functions in distance learning institutions?
explanation: Examination in distance learning institutions serves functions such as certification, selection, and accountability.

question_text: How many chapters are typically included in the final report of a research project or thesis, per the format given in this unit?
explanation: The final research project/thesis report has five chapters: Introduction, Review of Related Literature, Methodology, Data Analysis, and Summary/Conclusion/Recommendations.

question_text: SIWES stands for and is a programme designed to:
option_a: Give students industrial skills and experience to supplement theoretical learning
explanation: SIWES (Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme) is designed to give students industrial skills and experience that supplement theoretical learning.

question_text: What is the minimum duration for a SIWES attachment for ITF funding, as stated in this unit?
explanation: The minimum duration for SIWES should normally be 24 weeks (6 months) at a stretch for ITF funding eligibility.

question_text: According to this unit, how does a practicum differ from an internship?
option_a: A practicum is full-time, an internship is part-time
option_b: A practicum is typically part-time field observation with limited task performance; internships are usually full-time
option_c: They are entirely identical with no differences
explanation: Practicums are field experiences (typically part-time, 2-3 times weekly) allowing observation and limited task participation, while internships are usually full-time.

question_text: According to Falayajo (2004), assessment is likely to result in improvement of learning only when certain conditions are met. Which of the following is one such condition?
option_a: The outcomes tested must be recognised and accepted as important objectives of the instructional programme
option_b: Assessment must never be planned in advance
option_c: Only summative assessment should ever be used
option_d: Assessment results should never be shared with students
explanation: Falayajo (2004) states outcomes being tested must be recognised and accepted as important objectives of the instructional programme, among other conditions.

question_text: Which purpose of assessment involves using results such as interviews, questionnaires, and aptitude tests to help students explore and prepare for a career?
explanation: Guidance and Counselling uses assessment (interviews, questionnaires, aptitude tests) to assist students in exploring, choosing, and preparing for careers.

question_text: According to this unit, who scores and grades a Computer-Marked Assignment (CMA) after a student completes it online?
explanation: In a CMA, after completion it is the computer that scores and awards the grade based on the student's online performance.

question_text: In-text/self-assessment activities are described in this unit as being:
option_a: Entirely separate from the instructional materials
option_b: Built into the instructional process itself
option_c: Only used at the very end of a course
option_d: Never useful for identifying learning gaps
explanation: Self-assessment activities are described as being in-built into the instructional process, helping learners reflect on content covered.

question_text: According to this unit, what should a student do if they use too much time on one difficult examination question?
option_a: Continue until it is finished no matter the cost
option_b: Spend commensurate time based on the marks allotted, and move to other questions if needed
option_d: Ask the invigilator to answer it for them
explanation: The unit warns against 'using time badly' -- spending too much time on one question reduces marks lost from other unanswered questions; time should match marks allotted.

question_text: Which of the following is listed among Northedge's (2010) elements of examination revision strategy?
option_b: Getting hold of past questions and making a revision timetable
explanation: Northedge (2010) lists getting hold of past questions, gathering notes, and making a revision timetable among examination revision strategies.

question_text: According to this unit, teaching practice is peculiar to students in which Faculty, and how long does it typically last?
explanation: Teaching practice is peculiar to students in the Faculty of Education, who go for six weeks of practical teaching.

question_text: According to this unit, what must be included in a report of practical/experimental work in the Faculty of Science?
option_a: Title, purpose, materials used, procedure, observations, precautions, inference, conclusion
option_b: Only a title and a signature
explanation: Practical reports for physical science experimental work require title, purpose, materials, procedure, observations, precautions, inference, and conclusion.

question_text: According to this unit, what is the purpose of the feedback given after a Tutor-Marked Assignment (TMA) is scored?
option_b: To strengthen areas of weakness identified
option_c: To disqualify the student from further study
option_d: TMAs receive no feedback at all
explanation: After marking a TMA, the facilitator makes comments and gives feedback to learners to strengthen areas of weakness.

question_text: Instructional-based assessment modes discussed in this unit consist mainly of which two forms?
explanation: This unit covers two forms of instructional-based assessment: in-text/self-assessment and tutor/computer-marked assignment.

question_text: According to this unit, what does 'poor presentation' in an exam answer refer to, as something to avoid?
option_b: Unstructured answers lacking paragraph division and illegible handwriting
explanation: Poor presentation refers to unstructured answers lacking paragraph division, writing in note form, and illegible handwriting -- all to be avoided.

question_text: According to this unit, who is required to sign off on a Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme (SIWES) logbook and reports before the programme is deemed passed?
option_b: The programme requires a satisfactory report, reviewed by the School Board of Studies and University Senate
option_c: Only the student signs their own report
option_d: Only the ITF signs the report
explanation: The SIWES programme is not deemed passed until a satisfactory report has been written and reviewed by the School Board of Studies and University Senate.
